If passed, it will replace the Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act and the Karnataka Ownership of Flats Act, both enacted more than five decades ago. It now says that a fully completed apartment project can have only one registered association, even if the project was developed in multiple phases. items.title: 18 yrs after eviction to build a national highway, Kochi residents still wait for justice
items.summary: “Today you can get from Kalamassery to the Kerala High Court in 20 to 30 minutes. We gave up our houses for the good of the people and I’m happy to be of service, but our sacrifice was met with violence and years of indifference,” says 69-year-old George AL. George’s family was among the 316 families evicted in 2008 for constructing National Highway 966A in Kochi. The Kerala government had carried out the eviction over nine village panchayats in order to build the four-lane highway connecting the Cochin Port to National Highway 544. However, the rehabilitation package announced has not been received in full by any of the affected people. While all the families have been allotted land on record, 192 of the allotted plots are uninhabitable. A large number of plots are allotted in marshy areas where construction is not possible. Further, none of 316 families have received a job promised to them by the Cochin Port Authority. The government also promised rent of Rs 5,000 until they move into their own homes. items.title: Bigg Boss Agnipariksha: When queer dignity becomes prime-time entertainment
items.summary: When reality television promises an “Agnipariksha” — a literal trial by fire — it rarely acknowledges who built the furnace, who controls the thermostat, or who profits from the burn. On August 15, the premiere episode of Bigg Boss Agnipariksha Season 2 , a spin-off show designed to filter contestants for Bigg Boss Telugu Season 10 , offered a textbook demonstration of how South Indian broadcast media treats marginalised identities. Hosted by Sreemukhi, alongside a judging panel comprising actors Navdeep, Abijeet and Bindu Madhavi, the audition stage was pitched as a high-stakes arena designed to test candidates’ resilience. But when popular digital creator ‘Uppal’ Balu walked onto the stage, the interrogation that followed was not an objective assessment of his potential. It was a public execution of dignity, meticulously packaged for prime-time consumption. For years, Balu has been a ubiquitous and highly visible figure on Telugu social media. items.title: How to Apply for a Credit Card With Minimal Documentation
items.summary: Getting a credit card no longer means collecting a file of papers or making repeated visits to a bank branch. Many card issuers have simplified the process, making it easier for eligible applicants to complete the formalities with only a few basic documents. The real challenge is not the paperwork but knowing what is actually required, who is eligible and how to avoid delays during the application process. A little preparation can make the experience smoother and improve the chances of approval. Before you apply for a credit card , it helps to understand what banks look for and how to keep your application complete from the beginning. Why Some Credit Card Applications Need Fewer Documents Financial institutions have simplified their verification process over the years. If your identity, address and income details can be verified through accepted records, the paperwork becomes much lighter. In many cases, the documents required depend on your employment type, income source and whether you already have a banking relationship with the credit card issuer.
